tagline: High ground above the Missouri, where Lewis and Clark wintered.
intro: Highway 200A runs between Washburn and Stanton through the Missouri River valley, keeping to the high ground above the winding river on the course of Lewis and Clark's journey, toward the wooded valleys where the Knife River comes in.

The expedition wintered near here in 1804 and 1805 in a triangular fort of cottonwood, with the cold dipping to 45 below. Sakakawea, a Shoshone captive from the Knife River villages, gave birth to her son that February, possibly at the fort, and carried him west with the party in the spring.

moments.title: Washburn
moments.text: Founded in 1882 near the site of Fort Mandan, which is now thought to lie under the river, with a replica of the fort built near the original ground.

moments.title: Fort Clark
moments.text: Lodge depressions and more than 800 unmarked graves are what remain of a Mandan village on the Missouri bluffs, emptied in 1837 when a steamboat brought smallpox.

moments.title: Knife River Indian Villages
moments.text: Half a mile north of Stanton, circles in the ground mark Hidatsa earth lodges up to 40 feet across, in the villages where Sakakawea lived.
